title: Why a global financial company replaced three data sources with one
content_md: Industry: Financial Services Role: Security Engineer Use case: Data consolidation, API ingestion, infrastructure data quality A Security Engineer at a global fintech was building an internal graph solution to map risk dynamically across their infrastructure. To do that, they needed external data they could pull directly into their own environment via API and combine with internal signals. Getting a complete picture of any given indicator meant querying three separate sources: one for DNS, one for WHOIS, and one for web scan data. Each had its own format, its own access method, and its own gaps. Correlating across all three manually was slow. Building automated pipelines across three different APIs added complexity that got in the way of the actual analysis. One Pipeline for Multiple Datasets Silent Push brings DNS, WHOIS, and web scan data together in a single platform, accessible through one API. For the analyst’s team, that meant replacing three separate integrations with one, and working with data that is already cross-referenced rather than needing to be reconciled after the fact.
